metrics.outcome: Done: the site is workable. Every done-when item passes with Audit's evidence and the render check is clean.
metrics.brief: Brew Lab, Indiranagar, Bengaluru. One-page site with menu, hours, location and pre-order for pickup. We want a big photo gallery of the cafe AND a detailed story section about each of our three coffee farms. Keep costs low.

estimate_vs_charged.name: Page shell, menu, hours, location and gallery

review.verdict: Clean one-cycle run: Requester questions were answered, all 9 done-when items passed, and the code check found no overflow, JS errors or broken links, but nothing was stressed (no counter, refusal, hold, conflict or fix).

identity.note: Asked the right facts in [2], recorded a checkable charter [8], and the close [25] named both warnings and that the form was not browser-tested. The drop question [5] re-asked what the Requester had already settled in [4] (no photos, use drawings). Did not offer extra budget to fix the warnings.

adaptation.note: Three workflows mapped to the done-when items [10], and it flagged that the 35 total leaves nothing for a fix. It proposed using 100% of the budget on a 'keep costs low' brief, and cited no record evidence.

priority.note: Granted all three at 35/35 and noted a fix would cost 8 [11]. It also said 'Run wf-shell first', which is the scheduling call its role file forbids. No counter was tried on a 'keep costs low' brief.

coordination.note: Stated its rule each time [13][16][19], held the single write lock, and passed on the #farms and #preorder ids that the W-1 nav depends on. No role overreach.

audit.note: Per-item verdicts plus two real findings (duplicate meta charset, button navigating the current tab) [24]. Its remark that a fix is unaffordable at 0/35 is resource talk that belongs to Priority. It did not test the form in a real browser.

W-1.note: Wrote shell, menu, hours, location and 6-drawing gallery [15], said 'by inspection, not browser-tested', and flagged the id dependency on later sections.

W-2.note: Three blocks using only the supplied facts, id="farms", honest report [18]. Stayed within the charter's no-invention rule.

W-3.note: Form, validation, wa.me/919845000000, pay-at-pickup and 15-minute notes [21] all pass. The one real defect (order button also navigates the current tab, F-3) sits in its section.

went_well: The code check [23] covered what builders could not: 360px and 1280px overflow, JS errors, links, form submit. Every builder said 'not browser-tested', so it was the only real verification.
No redirects, invalid moves or validator refusals across 8 agents; workflows ran in dependency order under one write lock.
Facts match the charter: WhatsApp number, 6 menu items with prices, 3 farm blocks with only supplied facts [4][18][21].
Identity disclosed what remained unverified at close [25].
problems: Priority named the run order in [11], against its role file. Code did not catch it (role_refusals 0).
Zero reserve: 35/35 spent with a cap of 70, so the two warnings were left unfixed on budget alone [24].
The charter-drop pause [5] cost the Requester a second round for a point already settled in [4]. 'Keep them in scope' was ambiguous when no photos or extra farm detail exist.
learnings: Test next: a budget below the sum of estimates (e.g. 25 vs 35). This run had 0 counters, refuses, holds and conflicts, so bargaining, HOLD and Identity rulings are untested.
Test next: seed a defect that fails a done-when item. The fix cycle, Audit-to-Adaptation rework and lesson saving never ran (lessons memory off), so those cannot be judged.
Change: add a code check or redirect for Priority naming run order, since a role breach passed with zero flags.
Change: either reserve a fix amount in the starting budget or have Identity offer 'add budget for fixes' when only warnings remain. Evidence is one run.

Check the metering: estimate equals charged for all three workflows (10, 10, 15). If charges simply copy the estimate, Priority's stop-loss and 'estimate vs known cost' are not being tested. This is an inference from the metrics, not confirmed.
Keep the mechanical render check as the evidence base. Agent claims 'by inspection' were never backed by a browser run.
